matrices.title: Gram-Positive vs. Gram-Negative Cell Wall Architecture
matrices.summary: Core structural and biochemical differences between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial envelopes (Table on Slide 15 & 18).
rows: Thick, multilayered sacculus (up to 40 layers); provides high osmotic protection [L1 p15, 24, 25]
Thin, single- or double-layered peptidoglycan sheet (1-2 layers) [L1 p15, 25]
**Present**: Asymmetric bilayer containing phospholipids and lipopolysaccharide [L1 p15, 20]
**Present** in outer membrane outer leaflet; toxic moiety is Lipid A [L1 p20, 23]
**Present**: Wall teichoic acids and membrane-anchored lipoteichoic acids; induce septic response [L1 p21, 27]
**Present**: Distinct compartment containing transport proteins and beta-lactamase enzymes [L1 p16, 18]
**Absent** (molecules diffuse through open peptidoglycan pores) [L1 p19]
**Present**: Transmembrane protein channels regulating passage of hydrophilic nutrients [L1 p19]
**Highly sensitive**: Lysozyme hydrolyzes beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds to produce protoplasts [L1 p36]
**Protected**: Outer membrane shields peptidoglycan from lysozyme [L1 p36]
Generally susceptible if non-beta-lactamase producing [L1 p31]
More resistant due to outer membrane barrier and periplasmic beta-lactamases [L1 p16, 31]

matrices.title: Comparison of DNA-Transfer Procedures (Slide 35)
matrices.summary: Direct reproduction of the comparison table from Lecture 2 Slide 35 comparing Conjugation, Transduction, and Transformation.
rows: DNA transferred directly from one bacterium to another via sex pilus bridge [L2 p26, 35]
Chromosomal or plasmid DNA (F factor, R plasmids) [L2 p26, 35]
DNA transferred by a bacterial virus (bacteriophage) from one cell to another [L2 p30, 35]
Any bacterial gene in generalized transduction (or specific genes in lysogenic conversion) [L2 p30, 31, 35]
Purified naked DNA taken up from extracellular environment by a competent cell [L2 p33, 35]
Any free DNA fragment (e.g. Griffith pneumococcal capsule transformation) [L2 p33, 34, 35]

matrices.title: Surface Virulence Factors in Bacterial Pathogenesis (Table 7-8)
matrices.summary: Direct reproduction of Table 7-8 from Lecture 5 Slide 49 cataloging surface virulence factors across major bacterial pathogens.
rows: Antiphagocytic surface fibril; determines serotype [L5 p49]
Binds IgG Fc region; prevents opsonization and complement activation [L5 p47, 49]
Antiphagocytic capsule; determines meningococcal serogroup [L5 p49]
Unique poly-D-glutamic acid capsule; antiphagocytic [L1 p42, L5 p49]
Antiphagocytic capsule; type b capsule used in conjugate vaccine [L5 p49]
Thick mucoid capsule preventing phagocytosis [L5 p49]
Mediates adherence to uroepithelial and intestinal cell receptors [L1 p48, L5 p49]
Antiphagocytic Vi surface antigen [L1 p42, L5 p49]
Surface virulence proteins essential for pathogenesis [L5 p49]

matrices.title: Bacterial Oxygen Response Classes & Detoxifying Enzymes (Table 6.1)
matrices.summary: Direct reproduction of Table 6.1 from Lecture 3 Slide 16 showing the oxygen requirements and enzyme profiles of bacterial groups.
rows: Required for growth; energy derived via aerobic respiration [L3 p15]
Utilizes O2 when available; ferments or respires anaerobically without O2 [L3 p15]
Toxic and lethal; lacks protective detoxifying enzymes [L3 p15]
Grows best at low oxygen concentrations (inhibited by 20% O2) [L3 p15]
Exclusively fermentative; tolerates O2 presence [L3 p15]
Certain lactic acid fermenting bacteria [L3 p15, 16]

matrices.title: Bacterial Endospores vs. Vegetative Cells
matrices.summary: Core morphological and physiological contrasts between dormant endospores and active vegetative cells from Lecture 1 Slides 52-54.
rows: Metabolically dormant; zero detectable respiration [L1 p52]
Metabolically active; continuous replication and protein synthesis [L1 p12]
**High** (up to 15% of spore dry weight; chelates calcium to dehydrate core) [L1 p52]
Low core hydration (10% to 25% water content) [L1 p52]
High hydration (75% to 80% water content) [L1 p12]
Survives 100°C boiling for hours; killed only by pressurized steam autoclaving at 121°C for 15-20 min [L1 p53]
Heat-sensitive; killed by boiling or pasteurization temperatures [L1 p53]
All bacterial species in their active growth form [L1 p8, 12]
